title: 9th Sitting of second session of 2026
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem (Eydhafushi) chaired part of the debate on the digital bills
summary: The sitting opened at 09:02 with attendance, the agenda and a committee membership announcement. Most of the first half was question time with the Minister of Arts, Culture and Heritage, Heena Waleed, on spending for the 60th Independence anniversary (about MVR 4.1 million, all in Malé), the National Museum, the Hukuru Miskiy minaret, UNESCO listing and film awards. The House then debated the government's Maldives 2.0 Digital Transformation Bill and Digital Identity Bill, with mostly government-side members in support and MDP members raising oversight and spending concerns. After a recess (10:29 to 11:00) debate began on a committee report on the Export-Import Act amendment, still ongoing at the end of this part. The text is partly garbled, so speaker gists are approximate. The second half of the sitting continued the debate on the Committee of the Whole House report on the bill to amend the Export Import Act (Law No. 31/79), which was submitted by Komandoo's member for the government. Several members spoke on the bill, discussing cigarette duty and prices (a pack falling from MVR 250 to MVR 130 was cited) and the economy, and the chair and members raised points of order asking speakers to stay on the report. The chamber then voted 68-0 (69 present) to pass a report on party representation in standing committees and 68-0 to pass the bill. The sitting was adjourned to Monday 6 July 2026 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, so speech gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Heena Waleed
positions: As Minister of Arts, Culture and Heritage, said about MVR 4.1 million was spent on the 60th Independence anniversary events, all in Malé.
Said the National Museum holds about 7,000 artefacts, has had no major repair, and a China-assisted project is being prepared.
Said the coral stone mosques' UNESCO file was submitted on 21 January, evaluation visits begin in September, listing expected late 2027.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked what has been spent on developing the National Museum and the NSPA budget, and for updates from the national heritage centre's studies.
Listed President Muizzu's election promises, asking who made each, and argued they had not been delivered and that the public does not accept the government.
Raised promises on tax cuts, jobs and revenue, saying they had not produced results; the chair repeatedly asked him to return to the report.
Suggested the ruling party should find a different leader ahead of 2028.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked the minister how much was spent on the 60th Independence anniversary events in Malé and other islands.
Asked about care for the ship replica at the Hukuru Miskiy grounds and the use of Darul Aathaar space as offices.
Backed the Export-Import bill report but worried policy changes are made without consulting affected parties.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported digitising services, saying records become transparent; the chair twice asked him to keep to the bill's topic.
Raised the Hanimaadhoo airport and a fuel storage dispute, arguing digitisation reduces human error.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked what is being done about the Hukuru Miskiy minaret, which he said looks faded.
Supported the Digital Identity Bill and thanked the sponsor, describing it as a secure online identity system.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Asked what heritage and culture projects are running or planned in Alif Alif atoll, including Mathiveri and Thoddoo.
Supported the Digital Transformation Bill, saying digital tools make services faster and should reduce corruption.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked about the interactive museum plan, reported damage at the Usgekolhu site, a traditional medicine garden, and building youth interest in heritage.
Said fixing the cigarette price will not solve the country's problems and that the public's main concern is the president; urged Hulhumale members to engage.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the bill as a technological shift, saying services from home would cut paper waste and administrative cost.
Said Parliament amends laws in response to public concerns, defended the duty change in the bill, and criticised earlier MDP governments' borrowing and spending.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill as part of the government's 2025 to 2028 digital-first plan and urged MDP members to back it.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said he does not oppose the bill but argued basic services such as water and sewerage in his constituency should come first.
Criticised unmet presidential pledges; the chair asked him to stay on the bill's subject.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said he is not opposed but questioned money spent on a software company from a water and sewerage budget.
Asked for Majlis oversight independent of ministers over the data held under the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the committee report on the Export-Import Act amendment, saying it is not meant to raise revenue.
Contrasted the current government's record with the previous MDP government on debt, the dollar and asset sales.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Raised a point of order that the report contained no solar panel matter and the member was not debating it.
Supported the report, saying a cigarette pack priced at MVR 250 would fall to MVR 130, and criticised earlier MDP governments' economic record.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the National Museum is badly deteriorated and asked whether any major repair has been done in past years.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Asked how far work has gone, and how long it will take, to get the coral stone mosques onto the UNESCO list.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked whether heritage sites are being documented so the public can easily get information about them.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked whether Nasr Day (3 November) will be marked in Kulhudhuffushi and given higher national status.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether Addu City could host a higher-category Independence Day event, given its link to independence, and whether a heritage care project continues.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked why the history around a mosque linked to Dhonbandaarain's mother is not clarified, when the Hukuru Miskiy grounds work ends, and about local tourism.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked whether a national film awards ceremony will be held this year, saying none has been held in recent years.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when the Lily House project in Kelaa will be finished and how Eid celebrations and Eid sports are managed.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the Digital Transformation Bill as a way to end the need for personal connections to get government services.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the Digital Identity Bill, saying the existing ID has no legal force and the bill would give it legal backing.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the Digital Identity Bill, noting it has 11 chapters covering service records, a digital wallet and personal data protection.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order that the speaker was discussing matters outside the report before the chamber.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Raised a point of order that false claims about RTL had been made in the chamber and asked that this be noted.

decisions: Chair announced Ameen Faisal (Kanditheemu) replaces Ahmed Shakir (Maavashu) on a committee, dated 30 June 2026.
Chair announced the report changing party representation on the decentralisation and environment/climate change committees would be put to a vote at vote time.
Debate on the Digital Transformation Bill and Digital Identity Bill continued without a vote in this part.
The House took a recess from 10:29 to 11:00.
Report on changes to party representation in standing committees passed 68-0.
Bill to amend the Export Import Act (Law No. 31/79) passed by the Majlis 68-0 as decided by the Committee of the Whole House.
Next sitting set for Monday 6 July 2026 at 9:00.
